quote: With the owner's real captured book served, every underlying holding ≥2 option legs renders as ONE collapsed row: the 9 loose option-leg rows become 5 ticker entries (4 collapsed groups + 1 lone leg).
why: The parenthetical is factually wrong against the captured book, and AC-1 is a ship-blocking `test`. `apps/api/tests/fixtures/broker/positions_raw.json` (`"captured": true`) holds 14 holdings: 5 STOCK + 9 OPTION, and the adapter suite pins that shape (`test_broker_adapter.py:295` asserts `len(book.positions) == 14`; `:331` asserts `{exact: 5, partial: 9, unrecognized: 0}`). The 9 option legs fall on FIVE tickers, but not 4+1: TSLA has 3 (`1061776505` long 10, `1062038045` short 4, `1062257958` long 4), AAPL has 2 (`1061783502` long 10, `1061810138` short 10), META has 2 (`1062622359` short 5, `1062651284` long 5), NVDA has 1 (`1058096497`) and PLTR has 1 (`1058322781`). That is **3 collapsed groups + 2 lone legs**, and it inherits the same error from the BRIEF's "4 apparent verticals + 1 lone NVDA call". Worth naming: TSLA is not a vertical at all — 10 long / 4 short / 4 long, mismatched sizes — which is the concrete on-book proof that a qty+opposite-side heuristic would mis-pair TODAY, not hypothetically. AAPL also holds a separate equity row (`913256135`), so it is the live case for AC-22.
proposal: Restate AC-1 as: the 9 loose option-leg rows become 5 ticker entries — 3 collapsed groups (TSLA 3 legs, AAPL 2, META 2) and 2 lone legs (NVDA, PLTR) — against a served book of 14 broker positions. If the owner's live book on 2026-08-05 genuinely differed from the 2026-08-03 capture, say which is authoritative for the test arm (see my ask to PM) rather than leaving a fixture-checkable AC asserting a count the fixture contradicts.

quote: Summed across a four-leg group, the visible difference is up to roughly four times what the owner saw row-by-row at the live verify.
why: Three problems, and the measured direction is the opposite of the claim. (a) There is no four-leg group on the captured book — the largest is TSLA at 3. (b) The residuals are SIGNED and therefore cancel as readily as they add, because the group net is Σ sign × unit_cost × mult × qty against Σ sign × total_cost. Measured per leg (Convexa minus Webull's own `total_cost`): NVDA +$1.00, PLTR $0.00, TSLA-long-A $0.00, AAPL-long $0.00, AAPL-short $0.00, TSLA-short +$1.00, TSLA-long-B −$1.00, META-short +$1.00, META-long +$2.00. So the PM's "$0–$2 per leg" is correct as a MEASUREMENT, but at group level the TSLA 3-leg group cancels to EXACTLY $0.00 (13,760.00 vs 13,760.00), AAPL cancels to $0.00 (3,850.00 vs 3,850.00), and the worst real gap is META at **$3.00** (3,805.00 vs 3,802.00) across 2 legs. (c) "$0–$2" is not the guard tolerance; the binding guard is `abs(unit_cost * mult * qty - total_cost) <= max(0.01, 0.005 * abs(total_cost))` (`webull_adapter.py:211-214`), which is PROPORTIONAL. On the NVDA row alone it permits up to $39.45. So the true worst-case bound for the TSLA group is Σ max(0.01, 0.5% × |total_cost|) ≈ $102.77, not $8. The copy therefore cannot promise a flat dollar band in either direction.
proposal: Drop the multiplier-of-four framing. State the mechanism instead: each leg's reconstruction is guaranteed to reproduce Webull's own `total_cost` to within 0.5% of that leg's cost, the group net is a signed sum so those residuals may cancel or accumulate, and on the owner's captured book the group-level differences are $0.00 (TSLA), $0.00 (AAPL) and $3.00 (META). If UX wants a number in the copy, it should be a percentage-of-cost statement, not a dollar band. This does not change my summing order — there is no summing order that reduces it, because the residual is fixed per leg before the group ever sees it.

quote: A `net debit / net credit` pair is spread vocabulary and would smuggle in through the label exactly the structure claim the feature bans.
why: The premise is contradicted by the shipped surface this feature nests inside. `brokerView.ts:213-216` already renders every broker position's net entry as `` `$${...} ${base.net_entry_basis === 'net_debit' ? 'debit' : 'credit'}` ``, and `BrokerPositionRow.tsx:314-317` puts that string in the visible `Net entry` cell — so `$7,890.00 debit` ships TODAY on a SINGLE-LEG NVDA row, where there is no structure to claim. Debit/credit names the direction of cash, not a shape. Two consequences of banning it at group level: (1) the group would contradict its own children in the same column — `$3,850.00` above `$6,920.00 debit` and `$3,070.00 credit`; (2) it breaks AC-8, because `net_entry_text` formats `Math.abs(base.net_entry_cost)` and the direction word is the ONLY carrier of sign, so "the owner can confirm it by adding the rows they can see" is unverifiable without it. Note that a group net CAN be a credit on this book's shape (AAPL: 6,920 − 3,070), so the case is live, not theoretical.
proposal: Keep the shipped grammar unchanged at group level: one figure, magnitude plus the direction word, exactly as the child rows already render it. The group struct carries `basis: 'net_debit' | 'net_credit'` because the sign must be representable; whether the rendered word is `debit`/`credit` or something else is UX's copy call, but the group and its children must use the SAME word, and some sign carrier is non-negotiable. If PM wants the word gone everywhere, that is a change to the shipped per-row surface and belongs in a separate change, not smuggled into this one.

quote: `—`, `not recorded` and `no basis` never render on a group row, and remain reachable on leg rows exactly as today.
why: AC-16 (ship-blocking, `test`) bans `—` on a group row; UX §5 renders exactly that literal in the group header's Qty cell, with a tooltip, and gives the reason: "Quantity is a **per-leg** fact... The fact does not apply at this level — which is exactly what `—` means. Never blank: a blank cell is indistinguishable from an interpolation bug in a screenshot." Both cannot hold. The mechanism that forces UX's hand is real: the shipped desktop row is a fixed 4-column grid whose second cell is `Qty` (`BrokerPositionRow.tsx:308-311`), and UX §3 puts the group header in that same grid so columns line up with the legs beneath. An occupied grid cell must render something, and an EMPTY cell is precisely what `[absent-is-not-none]` forbids. `—` (not applicable) is the correct member of the five-literal vocabulary for a fact that does not exist at this level — the same literal, for the same reason, that the sim book already uses. PM's own ruling 1 ("It shows **no quantity**") is satisfied by `—`, which is not a quantity figure; only AC-16's phrasing conflicts.
proposal: Narrow AC-16 to the slots it is actually protecting: on a group row, the NET ENTRY and MODELED P/L slots may render only `not provided` or `unavailable`; `not recorded` renders nowhere on any broker surface; `no basis` renders nowhere at group level (see my self-revision below, which removes the group percent entirely). Add `—` to the group's permitted vocabulary for the qty slot ONLY, as not-applicable, and make its presence there a positive assertion rather than a banned one — otherwise the ban and the layout are decided by whichever spec the executor reads second.

quote:
entry_known     : boolean                      // AND over members
  multiplier_known: boolean                      // AND over members
why: A pair of AND-booleans cannot support an outcome I ruled and UX has already written copy for. My AC-17 requires that beside a withheld net the group states HOW MANY of its legs are missing the fact, and UX's §6.4 strings say "1 of these 4 legs" — a count, because "the short leg" would be a guess. A boolean says only that at least one leg is missing something; it cannot produce the number, and it cannot distinguish the two causes the permanence-first rule (which the same position states in §6.2) has to arbitrate between. UX's own assumption on the architect asks for exactly this and is falsified by the struct as drafted: "*Falsified if* the layer surfaces only a single `entry_known` boolean". I am raising it rather than narrowing my AC, because AC-17 is the criterion that makes a whole group's numbers vanishing at once read as a refusal to net rather than as a failure to read — the first time that cascade fires on the real book it will look broken, and "1 of these 4" is the only thing that says otherwise.
proposal: Carry, alongside the booleans, the counts the copy and AC-17 need: how many CONTRIBUTING legs had a never-supplied cost basis, how many had an unparseable one, and the contributing-leg total (already present as `leg_count`). Derive the group's literal from those causes rather than from an AND. If a composed `BrokerPositionView` does not expose the per-leg cause, the fix is a narrow read of the member's typed cause — not a re-projection through `buildPositionView`, which the same position rightly rejects for manufacturing a name, a qty and a max_loss. If the cause genuinely is not reachable without re-projection, tell me at R3 and I will re-cut AC-17 rather than have the copy invent a number.

quote: PM will accept that a group-level percent uses `plPctStateOf` unchanged and can therefore render `no basis` on a near-zero net.
why: Falsified, and 2 of 3 positions already rule the other way. My R1 puts "group-level quantity, percent return" in Out (v1) and my §5 states that `no basis` has no group-level occurrence in v1 because there is no group percent and therefore no denominator; UX §5 independently marks `no basis` "Deliberately unreachable at group level" and renders no `%`. So no group-level percent is RENDERED in v1, and a literal that cannot render is not a literal the group has. I have no objection to the group struct computing `pl_pct` via `plPctStateOf` — calling it rather than reimplementing it is the right instinct and keeps the fifth literal from drifting the day a percent IS wanted. The objection is only to it reaching a render, which is what "can therefore render" claims.
proposal: Keep `plPctStateOf` as the single authority and, if the field is carried, carry it unrendered. The observable: no percent figure and no `no basis` literal renders on a group row in v1. A per-group percent stays Future-dated behind the thing that actually blocks it — a signed near-zero denominator having a stated meaning — and when it lands, `no basis` is its literal and nothing else is. If carrying a computed-but-unrendered field is the kind of dead weight a later refactor renders by accident, drop the field; I care about the render, not the struct.
